newsitem.title: USA: GLICKMAN SAYS ETHANOL TAX BREAKS NEEDED UNTIL 2007.
newsitem.headline: GLICKMAN SAYS ETHANOL TAX BREAKS NEEDED UNTIL 2007.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department Secretary Dan Glickman said on Tuesday that the Clinton Administration will fight hard to extend ethanol tax breaks for another 10 years.
"This administration strongly supports Senator Durbin's objectives to extend ethanol incentives until 2007," Glickman said in a speech at the Illinois State Fair.
"The energy situation is no better now than it was 10 or 15 years ago. Ethanol is the primary means we have today to provide an alternative," Glickman said.
Senator Dick Durbin (D-Ill.), speaking before Glickman, said he would introduce an amendment to U.S. highway legislation to extend ethanol production incentives.
Senator William Archer (R-Tex.), chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee, led an unsuccessful fight last month to eliminate the subsidy in the budget bill.
The current subsidy scheme expires in the year 2000.

Energy companies now get a tax credit of 5.4 cents a gallon when they blend ethanol with gasoline. The tax break is worth millions of dollars a year to farmers, with about five percent of the U.S. corn crop used annually to produce ethanol.
Illinois is the number two corn producing state.
